builds.title: What did theropods eat like?
builds.notes: Title. Fossil gut contents are the only direct record of what extinct predators ate. Tonight: how to compare them to living animals without pretending one stomach is a diet.

builds.title: One gut is one meal
builds.notes: Compsognathus with Bavarisaurus in its gut. One predator, one prey, one point: a meal about half a percent of its own mass.

builds.title: One gut is one meal
builds.notes: Lanius excubitor: every recorded meal, 99 records from 4 studies. Of these living predators, this is the worst match to the Compsognathus meal as a share of body mass.

builds.title: One gut is one meal
builds.notes: Salvator merianae: every recorded meal, 281 records from 4 studies. Match to the Compsognathus meal, 2 of 6 from worst.

builds.title: One gut is one meal
builds.notes: Strix aluco: every recorded meal, 8437 records from 35 studies. Match to the Compsognathus meal, 3 of 6 from worst.

builds.title: One gut is one meal
builds.notes: Vulpes vulpes: every recorded meal, 2268 records from 85 studies. Match to the Compsognathus meal, 4 of 6 from worst.

builds.title: One gut is one meal
builds.notes: Alligator mississippiensis: every recorded meal, 152 records from 6 studies. Match to the Compsognathus meal, 5 of 6 from worst.

builds.title: One gut is one meal
builds.notes: Morelia spilota: every recorded meal, 77 records from 5 studies. The best match of the six. Even so, the fossil is one draw from a spindle like this, and we do not know where in it the draw fell.

builds.title: Borrowing from relatives is pooling
builds.notes: Three clades on their own. Crocodylians: six species. Iguanians: 47 records. Strigiforms: 29,448 records. Each line is what the clade says about itself alone. The dashed line is all tetrapods together.

builds.title: Borrowing from relatives is pooling
builds.notes: Now let each clade borrow from the rest. Thin clades slide toward the shared line, because their own data cannot hold them far from it. Strigiforms barely move: 29,000 records do not need help. Nobody estimates Scipionyx from one hatchling alone; this is that reasoning written down.

builds.title: The names are rules for whom to borrow from
builds.notes: Iguanians on the right: 22 species, 47 records. On the left, the clades we can borrow from. Rule one: borrow from nobody. The line is the iguanians alone. (No pooling.)

builds.title: The names are rules for whom to borrow from
builds.notes: Rule two: borrow from everybody equally. Every clade counts the same, birds and snakes and cats alike. In comparative-methods language this is white noise around a shared mean, or an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model with one optimum and strong pull.

builds.title: The names are rules for whom to borrow from
builds.notes: Rule three: borrow from relatives, more from closer ones. Other squamates count most for an iguanian, archosaurs less, mammals not at all. That is Brownian motion.

builds.title: The tree predicts first
builds.notes: Before any fossil: theropods sit on the bird stem, between crocodylians and birds. The tree turns that position into a prediction.

builds.title: The tree predicts first
builds.notes: This band is where a new theropod lineage should fall, borrowing from birds and crocodylians by shared history. It is wide, and that is the honest answer: close relatives in the living data scale differently, so the tree cannot narrow it much.

builds.title: The tree predicts first
builds.notes: Now the fossils: every non-avian theropod gut with a prey mass or bracket. Bars are prey known only to within a bracket.

builds.title: Microraptor: one genus, four kinds of prey
builds.notes: Microraptor: four gut records from one genus, a bird, a fish, a mammal and a lizard. The best fossil case for diet breadth: the spread of these four is the closest thing we have to a fossil spindle.

builds.title: Juvenile Gorgosaurus: prey about 3% of its mass
builds.notes: A juvenile Gorgosaurus with two young Citipes in its gut. Each is about 3% of the predator’s mass. Juvenile tyrannosaurs were not eating like adults.

builds.title: Sinocalliopteryx: about 8%
builds.notes: Sinocalliopteryx with a Sinornithosaurus leg in its gut: a dromaeosaur about 8% of its mass.

builds.title: Velociraptor: a fight, not a meal
builds.notes: Velociraptor locked with Protoceratops. The prey is heavier than the predator. This is a fight, not a meal, and it goes in the model as a direct observation, not a stomach.

builds.title: Theropods against every living diet
builds.notes: Every living predator species with at least 20 vertebrate prey records: 308 spindles. Colour is the major clade: birds, mammals, squamates, and the one crocodylian with enough records. Snakes sit low and flat; cats climb steeply; owls are narrow; canids are wide.

builds.title: Theropods against every living diet
builds.notes: And the theropod gut records on top. They fall inside the living cloud, mostly in its lower half for their size, and no single colour owns them.

builds.title: Fits along the tree, theropods beside them
builds.notes: Each living group at its typical size: the dot is the median meal as a share of predator mass, the bar is where 80 percent of a new species' meals would fall. Colour is the major clade. Pale with a triangle: a group whose scaling clearly differs from its clade. Hawks and cats steeper, owls and snakes shallower.

builds.title: Fits along the tree, theropods beside them
builds.notes: The theropods on their own dated tree, every gut record as a share of its predator. Tyrannosaurids, compsognathids, paravians. They spread across the same range as the living groups, and the spread within one genus, Microraptor, is as wide as a whole living clade.

builds.title: Which living animals do they eat like?
builds.notes: For all theropods, then each theropod clade: support for each living group as the source of the records, and for the dated dinosaur tree, all given equal odds beforehand. The dashed line is "cannot tell": every option equal. Paravians lean toward the tree; compsognathids toward crocodylians and squamates; tyrannosaurids, four records, are flat. None of these is far from the line. The model is telling us how little these records can say, which a regression line through eleven taxa never would.

builds.title: Close relatives scale differently
builds.notes: Slope of prey mass on predator mass for each living group. Feliforms: prey mass rises faster than predator mass. Caniforms: about in step. Sister groups, different answers.

builds.title: Close relatives scale differently
builds.notes: Accipitriforms against strigiforms: the same split inside birds. The model found this from data. It did not assume the tree was right, and it is why the tree cannot predict theropods tightly.
